## Timing correction: WMI events are batched; log receipt is not execution time

[Native-events run 34358925166](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34358925166) passed. The previously failed spend-rollup case passed at 318.48ms; GAP2180 passed at 114.70ms. No remaining timeout cause or class closure is established.

The post-suite control **disproved using WMI event-generation timestamps as precise process lifetimes**. Recorded cmd PID7272 had already exited with status23 by `13:53:37.0572738Z`. WMI subsequently assigned its start and stop events `13:53:37.5900451Z` and `13:53:37.5900452Z`, just 100ns apart. Both arrived at the collector around `37.797Z`. The exact PID and exit23 were captured, but provider batching makes their timestamp difference unsuitable as runtime.

The real tar records show the same limitation. PID5360's application log records spawn completion at `13:50:55.207Z` and successful process-exit observation at `55.364Z`; its WMI stop event was generated at `56.4508815Z`, over a second **after Bun already observed exit**. Two subsequent tar processes also received near-identical batched start/stop timestamps. Their application exit observations were successful/expected (0,1,0 across the three tests). This does not support delayed Bun notification.

Further corrections:

- GitHub's surrounding log timestamp for PID5360's exit record is `13:50:59.7877793Z`, roughly 4.4 seconds later than the application's own `time` field. **Log receipt timestamps cannot precisely align tests or file headers with native process activity.** The earlier proposed PID7036/subrun-header association and failed-test time window are therefore heuristic, not an authoritative attribution. The native CPU samples themselves remain valid observations of that PID's incarnation.
- The capture contains 2,075 start events and 2,009 stop events. This is not proof of complete process coverage or outstanding live children. Stops have parentPid0 in the examined records; ancestry must come from matched starts, while accounting for PID reuse and missing events.
- Snapshot absence remains insufficient to infer termination. WMI event collection adds process identity and exit-status evidence, but the control establishes that it cannot supply the required precise lifetime measurement here.

Another identical WMI round would not resolve this measurement limitation. If native lifetime is needed to attribute a recurrence, the next candidate is a controlled ETW/kernel timestamp capture whose event-time semantics are first validated against a known process lifetime. No application change is justified by this passing run.

Artifacts: `/tmp/archon-class-operations/native-events-34358925166` and `/tmp/archon-class-operations/native-events-windows.log`. These corrections apply to interpretation of the prior native reports; the [finite class map](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/issues/2924#issuecomment-5601658000) and both tracking issues remain open.

## GAP2180 sample: the log decodes exactly, `children: 0` is teardown debris, and the route's application cost is named

Attributed to the GAP2180 source/executor lifecycle row of the [finite ownership map](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/issues/2924#issuecomment-5601658000), discharging its experiment-matrix row for capture/executor versus cleanup ("time discovery, source preparation/copy/digest, child result and disposal on the GAP path"). Diagnosis only. Nothing implemented, no branch touched.

Sample: [job 102410119415](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34334328677/job/102410119415), head `04e91123c` (PR #3256). #3256 changes nothing under `packages/workflows`, and the test body is byte-identical between its merge base `bf554a782` and dev `0add05881`.

### 1. The log line decodes, and the trailing assertion carries no product information

Reproduced on Bun 1.4.2 with three controls, outside the repo:

| control | printed |
|---|---|
| body over budget, hook fast | `[802.24ms]`, `^ this test timed out after 500ms.`, plus `# Unhandled error between tests` |
| body fast, hook over 5000 ms | `[5052.52ms]`, `^ a beforeEach/afterEach hook timed out for this test.`, no unhandled error |
| body over budget AND hook over 5000 ms | `[10002.51ms]`, `^ a beforeEach/afterEach hook timed out for this test.`, plus `# Unhandled error between tests` carrying `Expected length: 2 / Received length: 0` |

CI printed `[10002.84ms]` with that third shape. The line therefore decomposes as body over 5000 ms *and* hook over 5000 ms. The hook caret wins over the body caret when both blow, which is why the hook label on its own never established a cleanup-only cause.

A trace probe pins the ordering the CI log does not stamp:

```
["body:start t=0","afterEach:start t=501","afterEach:end t=802 bodyStillRunning=true","body:afterSleep t=1502"]
```

Bun does not cancel an abandoned body. The `afterEach` starts at the instant the budget expires and runs concurrently with the still-running body.

What that means for this sample. The block sets `ARCHON_HOME = join(cwd, 'home')` at `subrun.test.ts:4328`, so the teardown `rm(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })` at `subrun.test.ts:4332` deletes the workflow tree *and* the in-flight staged captures while the abandoned body is still inside `executeWorkflow`. `expect(children).toHaveLength(2) / Received length: 0` ran against a deleted tree. It is post-timeout debris, not evidence of a child-creation defect, and the map's GAP2180 row should stop carrying "late zero-child assertion" as an unexplained signal.

That raw `rm` is also the most plausible reason the hook needed over 5000 ms of its own: on Windows it is deleting directories whose files two concurrent captures still hold open, which is the EPERM/EBUSY path. It is one of the 8 sites frozen for this file in `LEGACY_RECURSIVE_CLEANUP` (`scripts/check-test-cleanup-drift.ts:382`). Switching it to `removeTempTree`/`trackTempRoots` fixes the hook half and the misleading message. It does not explain the body.

Two toolkit notes worth adding to this issue. An explicit per-test timeout does not extend that test's hooks: hooks keep the 5000 ms default, so the neighbour's `}, 20000)` protects its body and nothing else. And that `}, 20000)` is not evidence that this route was known to be slow. Its docblock (`subrun.test.ts:4605-4608`) says it exists because the test's own `RendezvousStore` holds each child's lock query for up to 5 s inside `executeWorkflow`'s lock guard, and that wait counts against the test clock. Different cause, and it does not transfer to GAP2180, which has no rendezvous.

### 2. Windows band and in-job controls

Eleven windows-latest samples of this test, scanned from job logs:

| head | GAP2180 | neighbour `GAP: concurrent fan-out` (4 spawns, real bash, `}, 20000)`) |
|---|---|---|
| `da459356` | 51.32 ms | 289.30 ms |
| `ea1441d7` | 50.75 ms | 306.75 ms |
| `58e64faf` | 55.27 ms | 407.00 ms |
| `0add0588` | 56.65 ms | 405.68 ms |
| `f65c4dda` | 67.09 ms | 264.48 ms |
| `0b9fd48b` | 67.29 ms | 427.80 ms |
| `507570d1` | 104.61 ms | 493.60 ms |
| `7cb35c26` | 108.71 ms | 405.62 ms |
| `99498376` | 114.70 ms | 437.73 ms |
| `6ed5a4f3` | 524.58 ms | 4229.23 ms |
| `bf554a78` | 2036.19 ms | 6744.21 ms |
| `04e91123` (fail) | over 5000 ms | 436.88 ms |

Two readings follow. The route has a heavy tail across the whole block, not one test: in the `bf554a78` job the same describe block ran `sub-run discovery is NOT cached` at 2713.56 ms, `repeated SIBLING sub-runs` at 4456.13 ms, `when: on a later pass` at 4091.71 ms and the neighbour at 6744.21 ms, and the neighbour survived only because of its explicit `}, 20000)`. And in the failing job the neighbour, which spawns four children through the same `runChildWorkflow` route and additionally spawns real bash, ran a normal 436.88 ms, so that job had no global stall to blame.

### 3. What the body actually costs, measured in situ

A counted copy of this suite (every `fs/promises` export wrapped, counters reset immediately before the test's `executeWorkflow` and dumped immediately after, with the file's own bundled-path mock left in place) gives the whole parent-plus-two-children call:

```
body=17.1ms  totalFsOps=171
{readdir:51, mkdir:27, lstat:16, stat:16, readFile:16, access:12,
 rm:10, realpath:10, copyFile:4, writeFile:4, rename:3, appendFile:2}
```

171 filesystem operations, about 74 per child spawn, to run two eight-line YAML files.

Measured ambient Windows amplification for this exact invocation, from CI logs: 2.15 s locally on macOS (100 tests), 20.23 s on a green windows-latest leg (100 tests), 83.18 s on the `bf554a78` leg (97 tests, pre-#3254). That is 9.4x to 38.7x versus local, with a 4x swing between two Windows legs an hour apart. Those numbers are measured. What stays inference is the mechanism: Defender interposing on file creation, no `fork`, and ten package suites sharing four vCPUs under `bun --filter --parallel` (#2306). I cannot observe that without a Windows runner.

### 4. The application cost on this route, and why the test does not pay it

`runChildWorkflow` performs two full source operations per child spawn:

- `packages/workflows/src/executor.ts:1227`, `prepareWorkflowSource` into `captureWorkflowSource`
- `packages/workflows/src/executor.ts:1248`, `discoverWorkflowsWithConfig` over that fresh capture

`captureWorkflowSource` (`workflow-source.ts:494`) copies three scopes with one mechanism. In a source build, `workflow-source.ts:523-534` copies `dirname(getDefaultWorkflowsPath())` and `dirname(getDefaultCommandsPath())`, which are the checkout's own `.archon/workflows` and `.archon/commands`, and then `digestTree` (`workflow-source.ts:440`) re-reads every copied byte to hash it. `copyTree` (`workflow-source.ts:314`) is fully serial: one `stat` per entry, one `realpath` per directory, one `copyFile` per file.

Measured on this checkout with an independent replica of both walks (warm macOS APFS, three iterations):

```
capture: copy=33.6ms digest=7.5ms rm=12.7ms | files=200 bytes=1,247,503
         ops: readdir=86 stat=240 realpath=40 copyFile=200 readFile=200   (766 ops)
```

766 filesystem operations, 200 file creations and 1.25 MB per child spawn, of which the bundled scope is about 99 percent, and none of it is the workflow under test.

Re-running the identical replica while another test suite was running on the same machine gives `copy=395.2ms` against `copy=33.6ms` idle, with byte-identical operation counts. A 12x swing from contention alone, on macOS, with nothing changed but neighbours. That is the mechanism I am attributing on Windows, demonstrated locally: the operation count is fixed by the code, the per-operation latency is not, and the only lever the code owns is the count. A binary build takes the other branch and writes 97 embedded files per capture instead (`materializeBundledDefaults`, `workflow-source.ts:383`), so both branches materialise an immutable build constant from scratch on every spawn.

The tree keeps growing. `.archon/workflows` held 49 files on 1 Jul, 64 on 20 Aug, 132 on 28 Aug and 154 today. It doubled in the week this issue was opened, and every capture on every route pays the increase.

`subrun.test.ts` is exempt from all of it. Since `28aa32ee0` (2026-08-27, verified an ancestor of the failing head) the file mocks `@archon/paths` to point both bundled getters at an empty temp directory, with a docblock naming this exact Windows 5000 ms problem. Restoring the real getters in a scratch copy takes the same call from 171 operations to roughly 1,700, a 10x increase.

The point is what that mock is. The only way to make this suite affordable was to lie to the application about where its bundled defaults live. `fixture-runner.test.ts:32-38` and `workflow-source.test.ts:24-30` carry the identical empty-bundled-root workaround, copied line for line; `dag-executor.test.ts` and `script-discovery.test.ts` point the same getters at nonexistent paths; and the `cli main-catch envelope` row on this issue was closed the same way, with #2922 switching a test to `--dry-run` after it "froze a 383-file workflow source before failing name resolution". That is five test-side workarounds and one ledger row for a single application cost, which is exactly the shape this issue's standing decision forbids. Suites with no workaround still pay it on every Windows leg (`executor.test.ts`, `executor-preamble.test.ts`, `dry-run.test.ts`, `cli.test.ts`, `workflow.test.ts`, the orchestrator suites), and so does every production fan-out.

### 5. Fix boundary

What should change. `captureWorkflowSource` treats three scopes with one mechanism, but only one of them can move under a run. The project scope is mutable and must be copied and digested per capture. The bundled scope is a build constant: nothing writes to `getSourceRepoRoot()/.archon` while the process runs. Materialise and digest it once per process or per build version and share those bytes into each capture, on both the source and the binary branch. Secondarily, `discoverWorkflowsWithConfig` at `executor.ts:1248` re-parses that same immutable catalogue per spawn; a memo keyed on the capture digest would collapse sibling spawns while still missing correctly whenever an author rewrites a slot mid-flight. The `LOCK: sub-run discovery is NOT cached across spawns in one run` test rewrites the slot between spawns, so it stays green under a digest-keyed memo.

What must not change.

- Late resolution. Discovery stays inside `runChildWorkflow` at spawn time. It is a constitutional affordance, recorded in the case-law table and locked by the enclosing `describe('workflow: late resolution is a deliberate affordance')`.
- Per-child capture from the live authoring root. `resolveChildDiscoveryRoot` (`workflow-source.ts:793`) resolves the child from the parent's origin rather than the parent's frozen copy, so a fan-out child cancelled at a gate can be recovered by editing the child workflow. Sharing one capture across a fan-out layer would break that.
- Bundled bytes present in the run's own capture. `workflow-source.ts:555-559` records why: it is what lets a paused run resume across an upgrade. Change how those bytes arrive, never whether they are there.
- The two-child, gate and path-lock assertions in this test.

Out of bounds as a fix for the sample, per this issue's standing decision: a budget bump, an explicit `}, 20000)`, or a Windows skip.

### 6. PR #3258

`gh pr diff 3258` moves `withCapturedSource` outward so the child source has one disposal owner across refusals. It leaves the number and position of `prepareWorkflowSource` and `discoverWorkflowsWithConfig` per spawn unchanged, so it neither helps nor hurts this cost. It also does not touch GAP2180's route, which the [detached-disposal partition](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/issues/2924#issuecomment-5602020164) already excluded.

### 7. Verdict

Budget-edge tail, not a discrete hang. The sample is a runner-floor residual, but the residual only holds because the file already carries a mock that should never have been needed.

The arithmetic that settles it: the body measures 17.1 ms locally, this test's worst *passing* Windows sample is 2036.19 ms (119x), and the budget is 5000 ms. The failure needs about 2.5x more than an already-observed passing sample, against a suite whose own Windows total swings 4x between legs. Nothing on this route has to hang for that to happen. My earlier reading, that the neighbour running a normal 436.88 ms in the same job proved a discrete per-test hang, does not survive the merge-base leg, where the whole block excursed together and this test reached 2036 ms.

Per this issue's bar for a residual declaration, the route's cost is measured above and the irreducible part is the contract. A `workflow:` child must freeze its own source at its own start from the parent's live authoring root, and must resolve its target late. With the bundled scope off the per-spawn path, about 74 operations against a three-file temp tree is what that contract costs.

The application finding stands independently of this sample. `captureWorkflowSource` materialises and re-hashes an immutable build constant on every child spawn, and the only reason this suite does not pay it is a `mock.module`. Removing it is worth doing for the suites and production fan-outs that still pay it, while being honest that it would not have changed this sample.

Suggested ledger action: keep the GAP2180 row open and restate it as a budget-edge tail on the child-spawn route with `children: 0` explained as teardown debris and a residual pending the capture-cost fix; open a separate row for the per-capture bundled-scope materialisation, which is a product cost rather than a test cost.

### 8. Remaining uncertainty

- No Windows measurement. The 9.4x to 38.7x amplification is measured from CI logs, but its mechanism is inference.
- No slow local iteration was caught, so a rare discrete stall on this route is not ruled out. What would settle it: a Windows leg carrying per-phase spans around `prepareWorkflowSource`, `discoverWorkflowsWithConfig`, the staged-capture rename and disposal for this test, captured when it exceeds about 2 s.
- The hook half is attributed by mechanism, teardown racing live capture handles under a raw recursive `rm`, not by observing the EPERM/EBUSY retry on Windows.

Cross-reference: #2306 for the `bun --filter --parallel` amplifier. Both issues stay open.

Addendum to the [GAP2180 analysis above](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/issues/2924#issuecomment-5614499869): the teardown finding in section 1 is not isolated to the `afterEach`. The same file's `afterAll` leaks a temp root on every run.

`subrun.test.ts` creates one `subrun-test-empty-bundled-<pid>` directory per process for the bundled-path mock and reclaims it at `subrun.test.ts:50-52` with an unawaited `void rm(bundledDefaultsRoot, { recursive: true, force: true }).catch(() => {})`. Nothing waits for it, so the process can exit first. On this machine there are currently **472** of those directories, spanning two days of local runs, and some are half-removed (the `defaults/` child survived, the parent did not), which is the fire-and-forget race made visible.

`fixture-runner.test.ts:34` builds the identical fixture and reclaims it correctly with `afterAll(() => removeTempTree(bundledDefaultsRoot))`. Same pattern, two spellings, one of which leaks. That is drift on the exact path `scripts/check-test-cleanup-drift.ts` exists to police, and the ledger currently freezes 8 raw-recursive-cleanup sites for this file (`check-test-cleanup-drift.ts:382`).

Not a cause of the timeout, and not worth its own issue. Recording it because it is the second teardown defect found in this file while attributing the sample, and because both have the same fix: use the owning primitive (`removeTempTree` / `trackTempRoots`) instead of a hand-rolled `rm`.

Closing control for the [GAP2180 analysis](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/issues/2924#issuecomment-5614499869), and the cleanest one available: the same commit, rerun, passes at the fast end of its band.

Run [34334328677](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34334328677) on head `04e91123c` has two attempts.

| | attempt 1 (job 102410119415) | attempt 2 (job 102770118402) |
|---|---|---|
| `GAP (#2180 Defect A)` | over 5000 ms, FAIL | **43.37 ms**, pass |
| neighbour `GAP: concurrent fan-out` | 436.88 ms | 237.27 ms |
| `subrun.test.ts` invocation total | 36.39 s | **13.85 s** |

Identical source, identical runner image, 21 hours apart. The test went from blowing a 5000 ms budget to 43.37 ms, which is the *fastest* of the thirteen windows-latest samples I have for it. The suite total halved and then some.

That settles the verdict in the analysis above. There is no discrete hang on this route to find: the same bytes produce 43 ms and over 5000 ms depending only on what else the runner is doing. The lever the code owns is the operation count, not the per-operation latency, which is why the named application defect (per-capture materialisation of the immutable bundled scope, 766 filesystem operations per child spawn) is worth removing even though it would not have changed this sample, since `subrun.test.ts` already mocks it away.

Side effect worth noting: because attempt 2 passed, run 34334328677 now reports success, so PR #3256's Test Suite check is green. I did not trigger that rerun and have not touched the PR.

## Two pre-#3256 Windows samples from PR #3224, one with three timeouts in a single leg

Both runs are on PR #3224's branch, whose base is `bde2930e4`. That is before #3256 (the #3225 telemetry-exit fix) merged at `cb34483ae` on 2026-09-10, so neither run tests that fix. The branch changes only pack YAML, prompts, one Python script, and the generated bundle; nothing in the diff touches the packages below. The ubuntu leg was green both times.

**[Run 34255053142](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34255053142)**, head `d3ba2aafa`, 2026-09-08 17:12 UTC, windows leg:

- `@archon/cli` `pre-dispatch gates --json error envelope > leaves the default home untouched when the gate opens the registry` at 5,661.05ms against the 5,000ms budget.

**[Run 34449030974](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34449030974)**, head `e72eeecc6`, 2026-09-10 07:23 UTC, windows leg, three cases in one leg:

- `@archon/cli` `downloadWebDist > verifies against the embedded hash without fetching checksums.txt` at 5,000.78ms; the log records `tar extraction was killed by SIGTERM after 5252ms without finishing (limit 60000ms)` from `serve.ts:330`. Same case as the ledger's reopened downloadWebDist row.
- `@archon/git` `cloneRepository > authenticates a real Git clone against an explicit HTTP port` at 15,017.82ms against 15,000ms.
- `@archon/isolation` `setuid/setgid/sticky bits are stripped from applied files` past 5,000ms.

Two of the three, the real git clone and the isolation file-mode case, never invoke the `archon` CLI, so the #3225 telemetry flush cannot be their cause. Whatever slowed that leg hit three packages within seconds of each other, which reads as runner-wide latency rather than a per-test defect.

Next samples: the failed job is being rerun as-is for a same-commit control, and the branch will then take `dev` with #3256 for a post-fix Windows sample. Both results will be added here.

Same-commit control: rerunning only the failed windows job of [run 34449030974](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34449030974) on `e72eeecc6` passed in 8m33s, all three cases included. Nothing changed between the attempts, so the three timeouts were runner latency on that leg, not the code under test. Next sample is the same branch after taking `dev` with #3256.

Post-#3256 sample from the same PR: [run 34450544015](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34450544015) on `5841712fc`, which is the #3224 branch after merging `dev` at `cb34483ae` with the telemetry-exit fix. Windows leg green first attempt in 9m50s; ubuntu 5m48s. One green sample after two red pre-fix samples and one green same-commit rerun. Not enough on its own to attribute the earlier reds to #3225, since two of the three timed-out cases never ran the CLI; it is one more row for the rolling ledger.

## downloadWebDist row: the stall is bounded to inside `tar`, the 60s bound has never fired, and its diagnostic was misattributing

Adding evidence to the `downloadWebDist` family row. **The windows stall itself is still unattributed** — I have no windows runner and I did not manufacture a cause. What is new is narrower and checkable: where the phase log now puts the stall, why the bound that was supposed to end it has never once fired, why its message was actively misleading the last four samples, and that the same defect class had a second home nobody had looked at.

### 1. The phase logging worked. The stall is inside the child.

[Run 34453098156, job 102793178688](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34453098156/job/102793178688) — PR #3277's windows leg, head `5696ab4752`, 2026-09-10. One test failed: `downloadWebDist > verifies against the embedded hash without fetching checksums.txt`, at 5001.78 ms. The other two real-`tar` tests in the same file passed.

```
08:09:58.5897  web_dist.archive_staged        bytes:129   durationMs:3
08:09:58.8593  web_dist.extract_spawned       tarPid:2656 durationMs:266   <- last event before the timeout
08:10:03.5869  killed 1 dangling process
08:10:03.5871  (fail) … timed out after 5000ms   [5001.78ms]
08:10:04.3023  web_dist.extract_stderr_drained             durationMs:5447  <- arrives AFTER the failure
08:10:04.3025  web_dist.extract_process_exited exitCode:143 durationMs:5447
08:10:04.3028  web_dist.extract_exited        exitCode:143 signalCode:"SIGTERM" durationMs:5447
```

`39ca30545` was built to bound the next sample to before-tar, during-tar, or after-tar. It did:

- **Before-tar is clean.** Temp-dir reset plus the staged write is 3 ms.
- **The spawn call is 266 ms**, against the 24 ms the code comment records for a healthy windows run. One sample, so this is a lead and not a finding — but it is 11x, and it is on the process-creation side.
- **During-tar is where the time goes.** After `extract_spawned` the log is silent for the rest of the test's life. The child had not exited, had not written stderr, and was not going to.

Two more facts fall out of the same trace, and both matter for the fix:

- **The child does die when it is killed, and windows does report the signal.** Bun's reaper killed it at 08:10:03.5869; the exit landed 717 ms later as `exitCode:143, signalCode:"SIGTERM"`. So a SIGTERM does reap a `tar` stalled in this state on windows, and Bun reports `signalCode` there. A bound that fires can end this.
- **Nothing about that kill came from Archon.**

### 2. Archon's 60s bound has never fired on this row, and could not have

`e507ac6d2` put `timeout: 60_000` on the `tar` child so `archon serve` could not hang forever. Right instinct, and it stays. But every sample on this row is from the windows **test** lane, where Bun's per-test budget is 5 000 ms — 12x shorter. The runner always kills `tar` first.

Four samples, all after `e507ac6d2` and after the phase-logging commit (ancestry checked with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`), all the *same* test:

| Date | Run / job | Head | Elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 09-09 09:14 | [34333542426 / 102407573789](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34333542426/job/102407573789) | `826e61e7f` | 5 000.50 ms |
| 09-09 13:09 | [34355310964 / 102478450620](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34355310964/job/102478450620) | `93697c0c5` (PR #3258) | 5 000.90 ms |
| 09-10 07:23 | [34449030974](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34449030974) | `e72eeecc6` | 5 000.78 ms (ledger-recorded; the original attempt's raw log was not recoverable after the rerun) |
| 09-10 08:03 | [34453098156 / 102793178688](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34453098156/job/102793178688) | `5696ab4752` (PR #3277) | 5 001.78 ms |

Every one is 5 000–6 023 ms. The 60 s bound is 55 seconds away in all of them. Two consequences:

- **No sample on this row is evidence about the bound**, in either direction. A green windows leg does not mean it works; a red one does not mean it failed.
- **The bound's own message was misattributing every one of them.** It branched on `proc.signalCode !== null` — the *platform's* account of how the child died — which is `SIGTERM` for our timeout and `SIGTERM` for the runner's. Here is what run 34453098156 actually printed:

  ```
  tar extraction was killed by SIGTERM after 5713ms without finishing (limit 60000ms)
  ```

  The elapsed time gives it away to a careful reader, but the line names our limit beside a kill that was not ours. Four samples have been read against a diagnostic that cannot tell "Archon gave up" from "something else killed it".

**Fixed:** the bound is now a parent-owned timer that sets a flag the parent owns. `boundFired` and "killed by something other than this process" are separate branches with separate messages. Reproduced locally by disabling the new branch — the old shape reappears verbatim:

```
tar extraction of /…/target-extract-stall.tmp.tar.gz was killed by SIGTERM after 253ms
without finishing, by something other than this process (its own limit is 250ms)
```

Bun's `timeout:` option is not broken — I probed it, since [`.archon/engineering.md`](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/blob/dev/.archon/engineering.md) treats a built-in as a claim until watched: Bun 1.4.2 on macOS, `timeout: 250` on a child that never exits gives `{"elapsedMs":255,"exitCode":143,"signalCode":"SIGTERM","killed":true}`. It kills correctly. It just cannot tell the parent that *it* was the killer.

### 3. The mechanism #2928 removed still had a second home, on the same windows leg

`#2928` replaced `stdin: <Uint8Array>` with `stdin: Bun.file(path)` in `serve.ts` because the array form makes the parent own a channel it has to pump. That was the last word on this row — but not the last copy of the shape in the repository.

`packages/server/src/scripts/generate-api-types.ts` still did exactly this:

```ts
const generator = Bun.spawn([process.execPath, GENERATOR_PATH], {
  stdin: new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(await response.json())),
  ...
});
```

Measured payload: **86 344 bytes**. A pipe buffer is 64 KiB, so this was never one write — the parent always had to pump at least twice and depend on the child draining. Reachable on the same runner this row is about:

- `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs `bun run check:api-types` in the `test` job, matrix `[ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]`.
- `bun run validate` runs it too, so a contributor's `validate` could hang with no output.

Neither has a per-test budget to convert a stall into a signal, which is probably why this never landed on the ledger: it would present as a job timeout, not as a member of this class.

(Correction to the sweep that pointed me at it: `generate-api-types.test.ts` does **not** spawn the generator — `#2931` moved that test in-process. The windows exposure is the `check:api-types` CI step and `validate`, not the test file.)

**Fixed in the same PR:** staged to a temp file, handed over as `Bun.file(...)`, same parent-owned bound, named timeout error, staging tree removed in `finally`. This was the only remaining `Uint8Array` stdin in the repository — 9 non-test `Bun.spawn` sites, 2 pass `stdin`, and the other (`packages/providers/src/claude/container-spawn.ts`) is a Node `spawn` stream passthrough for the SDK transport, not a one-shot payload.

### 4. Footnote on the instrument: the logger mock does not suppress the phase events

Worth recording since the phase log is now this row's instrument. `serve.test.ts` mocks `@archon/paths`'s `createLogger` to a no-op, yet the real pino JSON events appear in every windows log. The mechanism is ESM binding capture: `serve.ts` runs `const log = createLogger('cli.serve')` at module evaluation, which happens on the hoisted import before `mock.module` takes effect, so `log` holds the real logger; call-time lookups like `getSourceWebDistDir()` read the namespace later and do get the mock. Fortunate rather than designed — but the events are trustworthy evidence, not artefacts.

### 5. What stays unproven

- **What `tar` is blocked on between spawn and exit is still unknown.** Defender path scanning is already falsified here (`071fcd6f2`: the runner image excludes `C:\` and `D:\` recursively, so the exclusion step changed nothing). No replacement suspect is proved. The 266 ms spawn call in the one raw sample points at process creation rather than extraction I/O, but that is one number from one run.
- **The bound remains unreachable in the test lane, by design.** 60 s against a 5 s budget: windows CI will keep reporting these as budget timeouts and this row should keep reading them that way. The value is chosen for a user's disk, not for a runner — 60 s is ~400x the 16–156 ms pass band.
- **What the fix does buy on this row:** the next windows sample will say which of the two happened instead of leaving it to be inferred from a signal number, and `archon serve` on a user's machine now ends the wait itself.

### Reading a future sample

- `Timed out extracting the web UI: …` → Archon gave up. The stall is real and lasted over 60 s. Also the first proof the bound can fire.
- `killed by … by something other than this process` → the runner or the operator killed it. Says nothing about the bound.
- Neither, plus a 5 000 ms test timeout → same as every sample on this row so far.

Row stays open. This closes "an unbounded wait can hide behind a plausible-looking diagnostic"; it does not close the windows stall.

### Addendum: there is no per-test extraction cost left to remove on this row

The standing lever on this issue is per-test spawn-cost reduction. Against this sample it has nothing to grip:

- The fixture is **129 bytes** and the healthy pass band is **16–156 ms**. There is no 5 s of extraction work to make cheaper.
- Pre-`tar` work is **3 ms**; the child then never reports exit at all, and dies 717 ms after the reaper kills it. A stall, not a cost — a smaller fixture cannot shorten a child that never finishes.
- All four samples are the *same* test, the first real-`tar` spawn in the process, whose own spawn call measured **266 ms against 24 ms** healthy. Cutting spawns from the other tests in the file would not touch the one that fails.

The only change that removes this test's exposure is deleting its real-`tar` spawn, which deletes the end-to-end proof that the extraction command works — and [#3189](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/pull/3189), now folded into [#3280](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/pull/3280), is a bug that only a real spawn catches (Git for Windows' GNU tar cannot parse the drive-letter operand, so extraction failed from Git Bash and worked from cmd). That is a coverage trade for the operator, not something to take quietly. Flagging it here rather than doing it.

Correction to the `downloadWebDist` family row: it describes an unbounded hang that no longer exists, and the stale text cost me a wrong diagnosis this morning.

The row and [issuecomment-5453633121](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/issues/2924#issuecomment-5453633121) both say the failure is "an unbounded product hang in `archon serve`" with "no upper bound". That was true when written. It was fixed by `e507ac6d2` on 2026-08-28, "fix(cli): bound the tar child and cover its failure cleanup". Current `serve.ts` defines `EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` at `:24`, passes `timeout: EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT_MS` on the spawn at `:237`, and names the limit in the error at `:291`.

So the product is bounded at 60 s. What still fails is narrower: the **test** budget is 5000 ms, and on a loaded Windows runner a real `tar` extraction sometimes exceeds it. The budget fires long before the product bound would. That is a test-cost problem on this route, not a hang.

Why this matters beyond bookkeeping: I briefed an implementer to "bound the extraction, unconditionally" on the strength of this row, and it would have added a second bound on top of `e507ac6d2`. Anyone reading the row today reaches the same wrong conclusion.

Today's sample, unchanged in shape: PR #3277 Windows leg, `verifies against the embedded hash without fetching checksums.txt`, 5001.78 ms, on a PR touching zero files in `packages/cli`. A rerun on the same head then failed on two different `cli.test.ts` tests instead. After #3259 landed, cutting that file from 43 spawns to 31, the same PR passed Windows first try. That sequence fits test cost, not a discrete hang.

Suggested row edit: keep the family open, restate it as "real `tar` spawn exceeds the 5000 ms test budget on a loaded Windows runner; product bounded at 60 s since `e507ac6d2`", and drop the unbounded-hang framing.
